toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The jump in chilled write-offs is most likely caused by the night receiving cut, not by Haverlow or the chambers. Since 27 July the night team has gone from six to four. Night pallets now sit on the unrefrigerated dock (about 15–17°C overnight) for a median of nearly 4 hours, up from 44 minutes. Trailer telematics show Haverlow loads arriving at 2.4–3.5°C with no alarms. The "warm" receiving probe readings are taken at receipt confirmation, after the long dock wait, so they measure dock warming and not what came off the trailer. The night write-off rate rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier, while day shift is flat. The chambers held temperature throughout.

Do not raise the Haverlow chargeback or move volume. It would penalise the wrong party. Do not drop night probing, which would hide the problem.

Next step: restore night receiving to six and set and monitor a maximum dock-to-chamber time for chilled pallets. Separately, sample Corriebank's claims against lots and receiving shift. The rise in credits is only loosely linked to their move to self-certified claims, and the extra warm-handled product may also be driving it. I'm fairly confident on the main cause. The credits question is unresolved.
